lesson.title: 911-Procedure 101 – Common Crime Definitions
objectives: Differentiate between robbery, burglary, larceny, and assault according to the procedure.
Identify key elements that must be present to classify a crime correctly.
Recognize when a crime involves force, threat, or unlawful entry.
Apply the correct crime category during call intake based on the caller’s description.

questions.stem: According to the Common Crime Definitions procedure, which key element MUST be present for an incident to be classified as a robbery?

choices.text: Property taken from a parked, unoccupied vehicle
Property taken from a person by force or threat of force
Property missing from a store shelf after closing
Property left behind in a taxi by mistake

questions.solution: The procedure defines robbery as property taken from a person or in their presence by force, threat of force, or intimidation.

questions.stem: Per the procedure, which scenario MOST clearly meets the definition of a burglary?

choices.text: Caller’s wallet taken from their hand after being shoved
Caller’s bike taken from a rack while they were at work
Unknown person enters a residence unlawfully and takes property
Caller left a bag on the train and it is gone now

questions.solution: The procedure defines burglary as the unlawful entry into a building or structure with intent to commit a crime inside.

questions.stem: According to the procedure, which of the following is BEST described as a larceny (theft) rather than a robbery or burglary?

choices.text: Caller was punched and their phone was taken from their hand
Caller’s package was taken from the locked lobby by someone who forced the door
Caller’s unattended bag was taken from a restaurant chair while they were at the table
Unknown person broke a window and entered the apartment

questions.solution: Larceny in the procedure is the unlawful taking of property without force, threat, or unlawful entry into a structure.

questions.stem: The procedure defines an assault as involving which of the following elements?

choices.text: Only property damage with no threat or injury to a person
Physical injury or attempted injury to a person
Breaking a window to enter an empty apartment
Any dispute between neighbors, even if verbal only

questions.solution: Assault involves causing or attempting to cause physical injury to another person, as described in the procedure.

questions.stem: Per the procedure, if there is NO force, threat, or intimidation used, the incident should NOT be classified as a robbery.
According to the Common Crime Definitions procedure, a burglary can occur even if no property is taken, as long as there was unlawful entry with intent to commit a crime inside.
If a caller believes they may have simply misplaced an item with no indication of unlawful taking, the procedure directs calltakers to treat it as a crime in progress.
Match each crime type to the key element emphasized in the Common Crime Definitions procedure.
answer: Property taken from a person by force or threat
Property taken without force or unlawful entry
Physical injury or attempted injury to a person

questions.stem: Using the procedure’s definitions, match each scenario to the MOST appropriate crime classification.
answer: Stranger punches caller and takes phone from hand
Unknown person found inside home with window forced open
Caller’s unattended purse gone from restaurant chair
Caller reports being punched during an argument, no property taken

questions.stem: According to the Common Crime Definitions procedure, a robbery requires that property be taken from a person or in their presence by use of __________ or threat of __________.
Which situation BEST matches the procedure’s definition of robbery?

choices.text: Someone takes a package from a porch when no one is home.
A person grabs a purse off a shoulder while threatening the caller with a knife.
A parked car is keyed overnight.
Money is missing from a wallet with no confrontation.

questions.solution: Robbery involves taking property from a person by use or threat of force.

questions.stem: According to the procedure, which BEST fits burglary?

choices.text: Caller’s phone is grabbed out of their hand on the street with no force.
Someone breaks a window and enters an apartment to steal property.
A wallet is pickpocketed in a crowded train.
Caller finds graffiti on their door.

questions.solution: Burglary involves unlawful entry into a structure with intent to commit a crime inside.

questions.stem: Which example MOST closely matches larceny according to the procedure?

choices.text: Caller is punched in the face during an argument.
Caller leaves a bag unattended and later finds it missing.
Someone drives a car into a storefront.
Neighbor is yelling loudly on the sidewalk.

questions.solution: Larceny is theft of property without force or unlawful entry.

questions.stem: Which call description is MOST likely to be classified as assault under the procedure?

choices.text: Caller reports someone is sending rude text messages.
Caller reports being punched and now has visible injury.
Caller reports a loud argument with no physical contact.
Caller reports a person staring at them in a store.

questions.solution: Assault generally involves physical injury or attempt to cause physical injury.

questions.stem: The procedure distinguishes between grand and petit larceny mainly based on:

choices.text: Whether the suspect is a stranger or family.
The type and value of the property taken.
The time of day when the theft occurred.
Whether the caller wants to press charges.

questions.solution: Grand vs petit larceny is primarily determined by the value/type of property under the procedure.

questions.stem: Which description BEST fits menacing rather than assault?

choices.text: Caller reports being hit with a bottle and bleeding.
Caller reports someone is waving a knife and threatening them but has not made physical contact.
Caller reports a car accident with property damage only.
Caller reports a neighbor playing loud music.

questions.solution: Menacing typically involves threats with a weapon or behavior that places someone in fear of injury, without actual physical injury yet.

questions.stem: The procedure uses criminal mischief for which type of incident?

choices.text: Property is intentionally damaged, such as windows broken or tires slashed.
Caller reports a stolen credit card with no damage.
Caller reports being followed home repeatedly.
Caller reports loud talking outside their window.

questions.solution: Criminal mischief deals with intentional damage to property per the procedure.

questions.stem: When classifying a possible hate crime, what is the calltaker’s main focus according to the procedure?

choices.text: Determining the exact charges on the phone.
Capturing the caller’s description of what was said or done, and any bias indicators.
Determining if the caller knows the penal law code.
Having the caller label it as a hate crime.

questions.solution: The calltaker should document statements, actions, and possible bias factors; classification is handled later by investigators.

questions.stem: Robbery always involves taking property directly from a person by the use or threat of force.
If there is no forced entry, the incident can never be considered burglary under the procedure.
Larceny generally involves theft without the use of force against the victim.
Criminal mischief is used for incidents where the main issue is damage to property.
Menacing may involve threats or weapons that place someone in fear of injury, even if no injury has occurred yet.
For classification, the calltaker should ignore any possible bias language or symbols and leave that to the responding officers.
Match each scenario with the MOST appropriate offense type according to the procedure.
answer: Property taken from caller with a punch to the face
Caller returns home and finds door forced, property missing
Caller’s unattended bike is missing from a rack
Caller reports car windows smashed overnight, nothing taken

questions.stem: Match each crime type to a key element emphasized in the procedure.
answer: Taking property from a person by force or threat
Unlawful entry into a building to commit a crime
Taking property without force or unlawful entry
Causing or attempting to cause physical injury

questions.stem: Match each factor to how it influences the way a call is classified.
answer: May elevate the seriousness or change the offense type
Supports classifying as burglary when combined with theft intent
Helps determine grand vs petit larceny
Relevant for assault vs harassment classification

questions.stem: Robbery involves taking property from a person by the use or threat of __________.
Burglary generally requires unlawful __________ into a building or dwelling with intent to commit a crime inside.
Larceny focuses on the unlawful taking of __________ without the use of force against the victim.
Criminal mischief covers incidents where the primary issue is intentional damage to __________.
Menacing may involve behavior that places someone in reasonable fear of physical __________.
